Surah 111 (Al-Masad / Al-Lahab), verses 1–5. Makkan.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Abu Lahab was the paternal uncle of the Prophet (ﷺ). He was extremely hostile to him and harmed him. He had no religion, and no zeal for kinship, may Allah curse him. So Allah censured him with this great censure, which is a disgrace upon him until the Day of Resurrection. He said:

{1} ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he.﴾ That is: his hands were lost and he was wretched. ﴿And perish he﴾: he gained nothing.

{2} ﴿His wealth did not avail him, nor what he earned.﴾ That is, the wealth he possessed; it made him insolent. Nor did ﴿what he earned﴾ avail him: it did not ward off from him anything of the punishment of Allah when it descended upon him.

{3–5} ﴿He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame,﴾ that is: the Fire will surround him from every side. ﴿And his wife, the carrier of firewood,﴾ She too was extremely harmful to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). She and her husband cooperated in sin and transgression, cast evil, and strove to the utmost of her ability to harm the Messenger (ﷺ), and she gathered burdens upon her back, in the position of one who gathers firewood, having prepared for it a rope around her neck, ﴿of twisted fiber﴾; that is, of palm fiber. Or it means that she will carry firewood into the Fire upon her husband, with a rope of twisted fiber hung around her neck.

In any case, in this surah there is a striking sign of the signs of Allah: Allah revealed this surah while Abu Lahab and his wife had not yet perished, and He informed that they would certainly be punished in the Fire. A necessary implication of this is that they would not embrace Islam. And so it happened exactly as the Knower of the unseen and the seen had declared.
